dbe_source.recommendation: In an exponential proof, factor out the smallest power. It is the common factor of every term.

lesson.concept: In an exponential proof, factor out the smallest power. It is the common factor of every term.
lesson.why: This is one of the highest-frequency errors DBE reported for this section.

example.problem: Show that 2*5^n - 5^(n+1) + 5^(n+2) is even for all positive integers n
work: Write each term with the smallest power 5^n:
This is a multiple of 2, so it is even.

probe.hint: See the example for the pattern.

learner_message: Factor out the smallest power — it is common to every term. Then simplify the bracket.
